deep.reconstruction:
The page opens a lecture course. A crossed-out first title reads 'specifische Wärme, allgemeine Theorie der Elasticität und mechanische Wärmetheorie'; it is replaced by 'Molecularmechanik (theoria motus moleculorum)'.

Riemann sets out the programme of mechanical explanation of nature:
- All motions in nature are to be reduced to motions of the smallest particles of matter, produced by attractions and repulsions between them.
- These forces fall into two groups.
  (a) Forces acting at sensible distances: gravitation and the attractions and repulsions of electric and magnetic bodies. The latter are 'very probably' reducible to attractions and repulsions between the electric particles of bodies.
  (b) Forces that decrease so fast with distance that they become imperceptible at any perceptible distance. On these depend cohesion and adhesion (marginal addition), elasticity, capillarity, and probably light and heat.
- The lectures will confine themselves to the mathematical treatment of group (b).
- For this he first needs general theorems of the mechanics of a system of material points, which he will derive.

Mathematical content:
- A sketch of a Cartesian frame (z vertical, x horizontal, y drawn obliquely) with mass points m_1, m_2, m_3.
- Point m_1 has coordinates x_1, y_1, z_1 as functions of time t.
- Newton's equations of motion for point i under the total force (X_i, Y_i, Z_i) acting on it:
  m_i d^2x_i/dt^2 = X_i,  m_i d^2y_i/dt^2 = Y_i,  m_i d^2z_i/dt^2 = Z_i,  for i = 1, 2, ..., n.
- Written out for i = 1, and begun for i = 2 (x-component only).

No derivation is carried out on this page; it only sets up notation.

The following page (context) continues in two ways:
- It forms Σ[m(ẍ)^2 − 2Xẍ + ...]. It shows by varying the accelerations, ẍ → ẍ + δẍ, that this quantity has the increment 2δẍ(mẍ − X) + m(δẍ)^2. Hence it is minimal exactly when Newton's equations hold. This is Gauss's principle of least constraint in its unconstrained form.
- It then introduces central pair forces m m' f(r) with a potential F, F' = −f. With P = ΣΣ m m' F(r), the force components are X_i = ∂P/∂x_i, and so on.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.
The second equation is unfinished: only the x-component for m_2 is written. The first symbol on its right-hand side was overwritten into X_2.
Some verbs in the prose are elided, e.g. 'lassen sich ... zurückführen' lacks 'zurückführen'. These are drafting slips, not substantive.

results.what: Programme of reducing all physics to central attractive/repulsive forces between particles, divided into long-range forces (gravitation, electricity, magnetism) and short-range molecular forces (cohesion, elasticity, capillarity, light, heat)
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (Opticks, Query 31); Boscovich; Laplace and the Laplacian school (Poisson, Navier, Cauchy)

results.what: Newton's equations of motion for a system of mass points in Cartesian components
results.modern_name: Newton's second law for an n-particle system

deep.surprise_reason: This is the routine opening of a lecture course on molecular mechanics: a statement of the Laplacian programme and Newton's equations for a point system. Riemann's lectures on gravitation, electricity and magnetism and on related physics are known, edited in part by Hattendorff. Nothing here is non-standard.

checkable.asserts: With constant force X, the equation m x'' = X gives x = X t^2/(2m) + C1 + C2 t. This is a sanity check of the equation form written on the page.

The increment of m a^2 − 2 X a under a → a + d is 2d(m a − X) + m d^2 (should simplify to 0). This is the next-page computation that the equations on this page serve: Gauss's least-constraint characterization.

transcription_corrections: The figure shows three coordinate axes: z vertical, x horizontal, and y drawn obliquely (the arrowed line ending in 'y'), plus mass points m_1, m_2, m_3. The 'y' is the oblique y-axis, not a separate point.

The penultimate sentence likely reads 'Wir bedürfen dazu einiger allgemeiner Sätze der Mechanik über die Bewegung eines Systems materieller Punkte, die ich zunächst ableiten will' rather than 'Wir beginnen dazu ...'.
'und diese letzteren lassen sich [?] wahrscheinlich' is likely 'sehr wahrscheinlich'. The sentence lacks its final verb (zurückführen).
'zerfallen in zwei [?] Gruppen' is plausibly 'zwei große Gruppen'.
'der Licht und der Wärme' is probably 'des Lichts und der Wärme'.

The marginal note to the right of the force paragraph is uncertain. It appears to read 'Die Fortpflanzung und Wirkung von Erscheinungen auf Bewegungen zwischen den Theilchen der Materie ... der Ferne auf einander wirkenden Abstoßungskräfte', with the last word possibly struck or altered. The given reading 'Ursache und Gesetze' is doubtful.
In the last line the left-hand side of the m_2 equation is written m_2 d^2x_2/dt^2 (the 'd^2' is cramped). The right-hand side X was overwritten into X_2.
